title: AC/DC on a Budget - Alternating Sparse Phases
abstract: arXiv:2610.27758v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: State-of-the-art neural network sparsification relies on alternating dense and sparse training phases. While computationally expensive, dense phases are critical for performance. Our empirical analysis reveals the mechanics behind this gain: upon reintroduction, previously masked parameters receive disproportionately large gradients that drive essential mask rewiring and parameter sign-flipping. Building on these insights, we optimize the performance-to-FLOPs Pareto frontier through three innovations: (1) zero-initializing masked parameters during dense phases to promote relevant sign flips, (2) shortening dense phases, and (3) replacing the dense phase entirely with a sparse rewiring phase that updates only the active mask and a small, high-gradient fraction of out-of-mask weights. translated_title: 预算有限的AC/DC——交替稀疏阶段
translated_abstract: 最先进的神经网络稀疏化方法依赖于密集训练阶段与稀疏训练阶段的交替进行。尽管密集阶段的计算成本高昂，但其对性能至关重要。我们的实证分析揭示了这一增益背后的机制：当重新引入时，之前被遮蔽的参数会接收到不成比例的大梯度，从而驱动关键的掩码重连和参数符号翻转。基于这些洞察，我们通过三项创新优化了性能与FLOPs之间的帕累托前沿：(1) 在密集阶段将遮蔽参数零初始化以促进相关的符号翻转；(2) 缩短密集阶段；(3) 完全用稀疏重连阶段取代密集阶段，该阶段仅更新活跃掩码以及掩码外权重中一小部分高梯度权重。在CIFAR100和ImageNet上的评估表明，我们的变体ARC（交替重连压缩）仅需一小部分计算量即可达到与基线AC/DC相当的性能。
tldr: 本文提出ARC方法，通过在密集阶段零初始化遮蔽参数、缩短密集阶段并用仅更新掩码和高梯度权重的稀疏重连阶段完全替代密集阶段，以极小的计算成本实现了与AC/DC稀疏化基线相当的性能。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes ARC, which matches baseline AC/DC sparsification performance at a fraction of the computational cost by zero-initializing masked parameters, shortening dense phases, and replacing them entirely with a sparse rewiring phase that updates only the active mask and high-gradient out-of-mask weights.
